--slab-concrete: #B6AF9C;
--ledger-manila: #D9D2B9;
--patina-rust: #9C4A24;
--oxidized-screen: #56624A;
--chalkboard-chalk: #F2EEE2;

Dark mode: background `--screen-ink`, primary text `--chalkboard-chalk`.
`--patina-rust` is the one accent in both modes, unchanged. Respect
`prefers-color-scheme`; do not force a single mode.

Four pages. See `page-plans/` for section-by-section detail on each.

1. `/` (Home) - `page-plans/home.md`
2. `/history` (About / The Ledger) - `page-plans/history.md`
3. `/menu` (What's Cold) - `page-plans/menu.md`
4. `/visit` (Hours, Directions, Contact) - `page-plans/visit.md`

Shared nav (all four pages, one line, max 72px tall): logo mark / wordmark
left, four links right (Home is implicit via logo, so nav shows History,
Menu, Visit), no hamburger needed at this link count but collapse to a
simple disclosure menu under 768px per the mobile rules below anyway, for
consistency with future page additions. Footer (all pages): address line,
hours summary, `[PHONE]` placeholder link, Yelp link, Facebook link,
one line stating "Sheffield's Ice House, open since 1942."

## Contact and unconfirmed data (hard rule)

There is no confirmed public phone number and no confirmed public email
for this business. Use the literal bracket placeholders `[PHONE]` and
`[BUSINESS EMAIL]` everywhere a contact detail would visibly appear to a
site visitor (footer, Visit page, any "Call us" button). Do not invent a
number. Do not mark either as a clickable `tel:`/`mailto:` link while it
is still a bracket placeholder, since that would ship a broken or fake

invent specific dish names, prices, or a fake-precise menu to fill space.

- Hero must fit the initial viewport on both mobile and desktop. Headline
  max 2 lines, subtext max 20 words and max 3 lines, primary CTA visible
  without scrolling.
- `min-h-[100dvh]` for the hero, never `h-screen`.
- Nav renders on one line at desktop, max 72px tall, collapses to a single
  disclosure/hamburger under 768px.
- Mobile breakpoint behavior is explicit per section in each page-plan
  file; every multi-column layout collapses to a strict single column
  (`w-full`, `px-4`) below 768px.

- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` disables the one hero settle animation;
  ship the reduced state, do not skip testing it.

- Dark mode and light mode both shipped and both tested, per
  `design-system.md`'s color mapping. Respect `prefers-color-scheme`, no
  forced single mode.
- One corner-radius system site-wide: `rounded-none` on containers and
  cards, `rounded-sm` on interactive controls only. No pill buttons.

## Definition of done for Loop 3

- All four pages built, responsive, both color modes tested.
- Zero em-dashes anywhere in shipped copy.
- Zero instances of a literal phone/email value other than the bracket
  placeholders in visible copy, and zero `telephone`/`email` keys in any
  JSON-LD block.
- Lighthouse mobile pass logged in the PR description.
- PR opened against `dev` per `github-workflow.md`, human review required
  before merge.

# Page Plan: History (`/history`, "The Ledger")

This page is the literal ledger device from `design-system.md`: dated
entries, plain language, only facts that came from the approved lead
research. No invented founders, no invented anecdotes, no fake-precise
dates beyond what is confirmed. Where the record has a gap, the page says
so, out loud, instead of filling it with fiction.

Layout families: (1) header statement, (2) vertical ledger/timeline list
(not a card grid, a real list because this content genuinely is
sequential, which is the one case `frontend-design` says numbered/dated
structure is earned), (3) full-width closing invitation.

## 1. Header statement

- Headline (display-lg): "The Ledger."
- Subtext (body-lg, max 20 words): "What we can confirm, in order. What
  we can't yet, we're leaving blank on purpose."

## 2. Ledger entries (vertical list, IBM Plex Mono dates, IBM Plex Sans
body, hairline divider between entries only, not a border on every single
line twice over)

- **1942** - Opens as an ice house in Houston. Screen walls, a concrete
  floor, cold beer. The idea has not changed since.
- **Recent years** - Named a Houston Press "Neighborhood Favorite"
  multiple times. (Note for the build agent: if the owner supplies exact
  years later, replace "recent years" with the real years. Do not invent
  specific years now.)
- **March 2026** - Yelp listing updated. Confirms Sheffield's is open and
  notes a recently refreshed menu.
- **Now** - Still pouring. Still the same screen walls. This page exists
  because it was time somebody wrote it down.

Below the last entry, one honest disclosure line (body-sm, muted color):
"This is the public record we could confirm. Eighty-two years holds a lot
more than four dates. If you're a regular and you've got a story, the
gap is yours to fill, not ours to guess at."

## 3. Closing invitation (full-width)

- Headline (display-md): "Eighty-two years, one afternoon at a time."
- Body (body-md): "Come add to the record. Cold beer, same screen walls,
  since 1942."
- CTA: "Get Directions" (same label and intent as Home, per the
  no-duplicate-intent rule; consistent CTA vocabulary site-wide).

## Components needed

A simple vertical list component (not a data table, not a card grid): a
left rail of IBM Plex Mono dates, a right column of IBM Plex Sans body
text, one hairline (`Oxidized Screen`, low opacity) between entries. No
icons needed on this page.

## Mobile collapse

The two-column ledger list (date rail + body) collapses to a single
column per entry: date on its own line above the body text, stacked, full
width, generous vertical gap between entries so it still reads as
discrete "entries" rather than one run-on paragraph.

# Page Plan: Menu (`/menu`, "What's Cold")

**Honesty constraint, read this before writing any copy for this page:**
the approved lead research confirms only that Yelp notes "a recently
refreshed menu" as of March 2026. There is no confirmed item-by-item menu.
This page ships with honest, category-level copy and a visible disclosure,
not an invented dish list. See `implementation.md`, "Menu content honesty
rule."

Layout families: (1) header statement, (2) category grid (bento-style,
exactly as many cells as categories, no filler cell), (3) disclosure
block, (4) closing CTA band.

## 1. Header statement

- Headline (display-lg): "What's Cold."
- Subtext (body-lg, max 20 words): "The short version of what's poured
  and plated. The full list changes; the cold part doesn't."

## 2. Category grid (exactly 4 cells, 4 real categories, no empty cell)

Each cell: category name (display-md), one line of plain description
(body-md), no invented prices, no invented specific dish names.

- **Ice Cold Beer** - "Domestic, import, whatever's coldest today.
  Ask what's on special."
- **Bar Snacks** - "The kind that go with beer. Nothing fussy."
- **From the Fryer** - "Hot, fast, built for a picnic table."
- **Something for the Table** - "Shareable plates for a full group.
  Ask what's running."

## 3. Disclosure block (body-sm, muted `Oxidized Screen` text on
`Slab Concrete` background, framed as a note, not hidden in a footer)

"This page describes the kind of menu an ice house like Sheffield's
serves, not a confirmed, current item list. We're publishing this ahead
of getting the real menu from the business so the site has something
honest to show visitors today. If you run Sheffield's and you're reading
this: send over the real menu and this page gets the exact list, same
day."

This line does double duty: it is honest with site visitors, and inside
the outreach pitch itself, it is a plain, low-pressure invitation for the
owner to respond. It reads as candid, not as filler.

## 4. Closing CTA band (full-width)

- Headline (display-md): "Come see what's cold today."
- CTA: "Get Directions" (same label/intent as Home and History, per the
  no-duplicate-intent rule).

## Components needed

Bento-style grid (`grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 gap-6`, four cells,
`rounded-none`, at least two cells get a real texture background per
`assets.md` rather than all four being flat text-only cells, satisfying
the bento background diversity rule with real content, not decoration for
its own sake).

## Mobile collapse

Category grid: single column, cells stack in the order listed above.
Disclosure block: full width, unchanged typographically, just narrower.

# Assets

## What exists

- Yelp listing (photos likely attached to the listing itself):
  `https://www.yelp.com/biz/sheffields-ice-house-houston-2`
- Facebook page (photos likely attached to the page):
  `https://www.facebook.com/p/Sheffields-Ice-House-100063498222755/`

**Rule for Loop 3:** do not scrape, download, or republish photos from
Yelp or Facebook without the business's explicit permission. Those photos
belong to the business or to reviewers, not to this project, and using
them without permission undermines the exact trust this site is trying to
build. If the owner grants access during outreach, real photos of the
actual building, screen walls, and patio are the single best asset this
site could use, and should replace the generated placeholders below at
that point. Until then, link out to Yelp and Facebook (as done on Home and
Visit) rather than embedding their images.

**Never invent a real staff or customer likeness.** No generated photo on
this site may depict a specific identifiable person standing in for a
real employee, owner, or regular. Generated imagery is limited to empty
spaces, textures, and objects: the building, the screen wall, a beer glass,
string lights, a concrete floor. If a generated image ever includes a
human figure, it must be an anonymous, non-identifiable silhouette or
crowd shot, never a posed "customer" or "bartender" character standing in
as if they were a real Sheffield's employee.

## What must be generated for v0

Use Pollinations (free image generation, per campaign convention) for
every placeholder image below. Each prompt is written to match
`design-system.md`'s materiality (matte concrete, oxidized screen mesh,
patina rust, string lights, no gloss, no neon) and to avoid depicting any
specific real person.

1. **Ink-stamp mark** (hero signature element, Home section 1). Not a
   photo, a flat graphic/SVG-style asset: a rubber-stamp impression
   reading "EST. 1942," slightly rotated, worn ink edges, rendered in
   `Patina Rust` on a `Ledger Manila` or transparent background. Pollinations
   prompt: "flat vector-style rubber stamp graphic, worn ink impression,
   text EST 1942, rust orange ink on aged paper texture, slightly
   rotated, no photorealism, no people, minimal illustration." If the
   generated result is not a clean flat mark, fall back to building it as
   actual CSS/SVG (a real `<svg>` stamp shape with `text` inside, rotated,
   given a rough edge via an SVG filter) rather than accepting a muddy
   generated image; this is exactly the kind of "single simple geometric
   mark" the anti-slop guidance allows as a hand-built SVG.
2. **Patio/screen-wall texture** (Home sections 3 and 4 background,
   Menu bento cell backgrounds). Pollinations prompt: "photo-realistic
   texture of a weathered aluminum window screen mesh over painted
   cinderblock wall, Gulf Coast humidity patina, soft afternoon light, no
   people, no text, no logos, empty scene."
3. **Concrete floor / string lights detail** (Menu bento cell, secondary
   texture). Pollinations prompt: "photo-realistic close shot of a
   painted concrete floor under string lights at dusk, empty outdoor bar
   patio, warm bulb glow, no people, no text, no logos."
4. **Beer glass, cold and sweating** (small supporting image, Home
   section 4 "What's Cold" or Menu header). Pollinations prompt:
   "photo-realistic single cold beer glass with condensation on a worn
   wood picnic table, outdoor daylight, no people, no hands, no logos, no
   text."

Generate each at the aspect ratio the section needs (roughly 16:9 for
section backgrounds, 1:1 or 4:3 for bento cells) rather than cropping one
shared image down for every placement, since a single reused image across
multiple sections would read as filler.

## Icons

`@phosphor-icons/react`, one stroke weight (`1.5`) site-wide, used only
for the Visit page's external-link indicators and the Home "Find Us"
cards. No hand-rolled icon SVGs; the one hand-built SVG on this site is
the ink-stamp mark above, which is decoration, not an icon.

## Logo / wordmark

No existing logo file was found in the lead research. v0 ships with a
text wordmark set in Big Shoulders Display, "Sheffield's Ice House," no
generated logo mark beyond the ink-stamp signature element above. If the

# User Flow

Two entry points, matching the two audiences in `brief.md`. Hand-written
per the option in the process brief (no `diagram-design` HTML artifact
needed for a four-page marketing site; a text flow is the right amount of
tool for this).

## Flow 1: The worried regular (checking if Sheffield's is still open)

```
Search "Sheffield's Ice House Houston"
        |
        v
  Lands on Home (/)
        |
        v
Reads hero: "Open Since 1942" + "82 years and counting"
        |
        v
Sees "Still Open" section directly rebutting the closed-listing doubt
        |
        v
   Decision point
        |
   +----+----------------------------+
   |                                 |
   v                                 v
Checks "Find Us" hours card     Skips straight to
on Home ( [HOURS] + link             Visit page for
to full Visit page )                 full hours/map
   |                                 |
   +----------------+----------------+
                     v
              Visit page (/visit)
                     |
                     v
        Clicks "Find on Map" CTA
                     |
                     v
        Google Maps opens, resolves
        Sheffield's by name and city
                     |
                     v
              Visitor drives over
```

Exit criteria for success: the visitor decides, within the hero and the
"Still Open" section alone, that the place is open, without needing to
read the History or Menu pages at all. Those pages are there for the
second audience, not required reading for this one.

## Flow 2: The curious newcomer (heard the name, never been)

```
Sees a Houston Press "Neighborhood Favorite" mention or hears
from a friend
        |
        v
  Searches the name, lands on Home (/)
        |
        v
Reads hero + "Still Open" (same as Flow 1, builds baseline trust)
        |
        v
   Curious, wants more context before committing to a visit
        |
        v
Clicks "Read the History" -> History page (/history)
        |
        v
Reads the ledger entries (1942, Houston Press mentions, March 2026 Yelp
update), trust deepens: this is a real, long-running place, not a
pop-up or a listing error
        |
        v
Clicks "See the Menu" (nav, not forced path) -> Menu page (/menu)
        |
        v
Sees category-level menu, understands what kind of place this is
(cold beer, bar snacks, no surprises), notes the honest disclosure
that the full item list is still being confirmed
        |
        v
Clicks "Get Directions" (repeated CTA label, same intent every time
it appears) -> Visit page (/visit)
        |
        v
Checks [HOURS] placeholder and the Yelp/Facebook links for the most
current info, clicks "Find on Map"
        |
        v
              Visitor plans a first trip
```

## Why one CTA label carries the whole flow

"Get Directions" appears on Home (hero and closing statement), History
(closing), and Menu (closing), always pointing at the same destination
and the same intent: get the visitor from "convinced" to "en route." The
Visit page itself uses "Find on Map" instead, since that page already is
the directions destination; repeating "Get Directions" there would be a
button pointing at the page it's already on. This is the one deliberate
label swap in the whole site, and it exists for a concrete reason, not for
variety's own sake.

# Handling Protocols

Operational rules for whoever (human or agent) picks this repo up next,
in this loop or a later one.

## File and folder naming

- Root-level planning docs stay flat and lowercase-hyphenated:
  `brief.md`, `implementation.md`, `design-system.md`, `assets.md`,
  `user-flow.md`, `handling-protocols.md`, `github-workflow.md`,
  `skills-used.md`, `README.md`.
- Page plans live in `page-plans/`, one file per route, named after the
  route's slug, not the page's display title: `home.md`, `history.md`,
  `menu.md`, `visit.md`. If a page is added later, its slug is the
  filename; do not name a file after a headline that might change.
- When Loop 3 starts the actual Next.js build, application code goes in
  a conventional `app/`, `components/`, `lib/` structure at the repo
  root, alongside these planning docs, not inside a new subfolder that
  buries the docs. The docs stay discoverable at the root.

## Context loss / resume-after-interruption

If this repo is picked back up cold (new session, no memory of this
Loop 2 run):

1. Read `README.md` first for status and campaign context.
2. Read `brief.md` for the business facts and the chosen direction.
3. Read `design-system.md` and `implementation.md` before writing or
   changing any code; they are the source of truth for the visual system
   and the hard build rules, respectively.
4. Check the repo's current branch and open PRs before assuming Loop 3
   hasn't started; `git log --oneline --all` and `gh pr list --state all`
   are the two commands to run before doing anything else.
5. Never re-invent the phone/email/hours placeholder policy from
   scratch. It is documented in `implementation.md` and exists precisely
   so a future session doesn't accidentally fabricate contact details
   that were never confirmed. Grep the repo for `[PHONE]`,
   `[BUSINESS EMAIL]`, and `[HOURS]` before touching any contact-related
   copy, to see every place the placeholder currently lives.

## Sandboxed visual testing via /browse

Once Loop 3 has a running local build, use the `/browse` skill (per this
account's global instruction: never `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` for this
kind of check) to load the site headless and verify:

- Hero fits the viewport at 375px, 768px, and 1440px widths, no scroll
  needed to see the primary CTA.
- Both color modes render with the six tokens from `design-system.md`,
  no stray colors.
- No literal phone/email/hours value leaked into the rendered HTML
  outside the three approved bracket placeholders.
- The "Find on Map" link resolves to the Google Maps search URL from
  `implementation.md`, not a dead link or a fabricated address.

Do not open a real browser session or a personal Chrome profile for this;
`/browse`'s headless daemon is the sandboxed, disposable option and
matches this account's standing instruction to avoid the Chrome MCP path.

## Token optimization

- Do not re-read every file in this repo at the start of every session.
  `README.md` plus the specific file needed for the task at hand is
  enough for most changes; `implementation.md` is the one file worth
  reading in full before any code change, since it holds the
  non-negotiable rules (placeholders, JSON-LD omissions, performance
  budget).
- When asking an agent to build one page, hand it only that page's
  `page-plans/*.md` file plus `design-system.md` and the relevant slice
  of `implementation.md`, not the entire repo's planning corpus.
- Prefer `git diff`/`git log -p` over re-reading whole files when
  checking what changed between sessions.

# Sheffield's Ice House, website plan

This repo is a **website plan**, not a built site. It is Loop 2 output
from the `website-pitch-pipeline` cold-outreach campaign: the design
direction, copy direction, page-by-page information architecture, and a
zero-follow-up-questions build brief for an 82-year-old Houston ice house
that currently has no website at all.

## Status

**pending-beta.** No application code exists yet. Everything in this repo
is planning: business brief, design system, page plans, copy direction,
asset plan, and the implementation brief Loop 3 will build from.

## Campaign

- Pipeline: `PIIIX-org/website-pitch-pipeline`
- Campaign: `texas-bars-batch-1`
- Geography: Texas, US (statewide campaign); this business is in Houston
- Locale: en (US English)
- Sibling repo in the same batch: `PIIIX-org/texas-bar-texan-drive-in`
  (The Texan Drive-In, Corpus Christi, a different design lane, do not
  cross-reference their contact placeholders with this business's)

## The business, in one paragraph

Sheffield's Ice House has been open in Houston since 1942, 82 years on
the same idea: screen walls, a concrete floor, cold beer, no pretense.
Houston Press has named it a neighborhood favorite in multiple recent
years, and its Yelp listing was updated in March 2026 confirming it is
still open with a recently refreshed menu. It has never had a website. A
Yellow Pages listing currently and incorrectly marks it as closed. This
site's job is to correct that record and give people a real reason to
show up.

## Contact info policy (read before touching any copy)

No confirmed public phone number or email exists for this business. Every
place a phone number or email would appear uses the literal placeholders
`[PHONE]` and `[BUSINESS EMAIL]`. No confirmed hours or street address
exist either; those use `[HOURS]` and a Google Maps search-query link
instead of a fabricated address, per `implementation.md`. Never replace
any of these with an invented value. See `implementation.md` for the full
rule, including why these must never appear as literal values inside
JSON-LD structured data.

## Repo map

| File | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `brief.md` | Business, audience, geography, offer, strengths/weaknesses, conversion goal, rejected directions |
| `design-system.md` | The "Ledger House" visual lane: colors, type, spacing, motion, tone, and why it doesn't overlap the other four businesses in this batch |
| `implementation.md` | Loop 3 build brief: stack, tokens, page structure, hard performance/mobile rules, placeholder and JSON-LD rules |
| `page-plans/` | One file per page: `home.md`, `history.md`, `menu.md`, `visit.md` |
| `assets.md` | What exists (Yelp/Facebook, not to be scraped without permission) vs. what to generate (Pollinations), and how |
| `user-flow.md` | Two visitor flows: the worried regular, the curious newcomer |
| `handling-protocols.md` | Naming, resume-after-interruption, sandboxed QA via `/browse`, token optimization |
| `github-workflow.md` | `dev`/`prod` branch strategy, PR flow, CI expectations, human review gate |
| `skills-used.md` | Which skills were invoked for which file, and the self-score for this Loop 2 pass |

## How to pick this back up

1. Read this file, then `brief.md`, then `design-system.md`.
2. Check `gh pr list --state all` and `git log --oneline --all` before
   assuming no work has started.
3. If starting Loop 3 (the actual build), read `implementation.md` in
   full first, it is the single source of truth for what must not be
   fabricated (contact details, hours, menu items) and what the hard
   performance/mobile rules are.
4. Follow `github-workflow.md` for branching; nothing merges to `dev`
   without human review, and `dev` to `prod` promotion is a separate,
   later, human-approved step.

# Brief: Sheffield's Ice House

## The business

Sheffield's Ice House. Houston, Texas. An ice house, the specific Texas bar
category: open-air or screened seating, cold beer, concrete floor, no
pretense. It has run continuously since 1942. That is 82 years on the same
plot, under the same idea, through the same Houston humidity.

Category note for anyone unfamiliar with the term: an ice house is not a
sports bar and not a dive bar dressed up as one. It started as a literal
ice-delivery depot with a beer license bolted on, and the form stuck: screen
walls instead of solid ones, a garage-door opening to the parking lot,
picnic tables, box fans, string lights after dark. Sheffield's is that
building, not a theme built to look like that building.

## Audience

Two audiences, in this order:

1. **Houston regulars and neighbors.** People who already know the name,
   have been going for years or decades, and need the site to do one thing:
   confirm the place is still open and tell them when to show up. This
   audience does not need to be sold. They need to stop worrying it closed.
2. **Newcomers and the recently-curious.** People who saw the Houston Press
   "Neighborhood Favorite" mention, or a friend told them about "that ice
   house that's been there forever," and searched for it. Right now they
   find nothing, or worse, a Yellow Pages listing telling them it's closed.
   The site's job for this group is to exist, look like it belongs to a
   real 82-year-old business, and get them in the door.

Geography: Houston, Texas, Gulf Coast humidity climate. This matters for
design (heat, shade, screen walls, box fans) and for copy (nobody in
Houston needs the concept of "hot" explained to them, so the site should
never over-explain it).

Locale: en (US English).

## The offer

There is no delivery app, no loyalty program, no online ordering. The offer
is the same offer it has been since 1942: come sit in the shade, drink a
cold beer, and be around other people doing the same thing. The site is not
selling a transaction. It is selling a location and a fact: we are open, we
have been for 82 years, come find out for yourself.

## Strengths (from lead research, Gate A approved)

- Operating continuously since 1942, 82 years on the same site.
- Named a Houston Press "Neighborhood Favorite" in multiple recent years.
- Yelp listing updated March 2026 confirms it is open and the menu was
  recently refreshed.

## Weaknesses (from lead research, Gate A approved)

- No website anywhere, for an 82-year-old, publicly recognized institution.
- A Yellow Pages listing incorrectly marks it as closed. This is not a
  hypothetical risk. It is an active, findable piece of misinformation
  sitting next to the real listings, and it is exactly the kind of thing a
  first-time visitor hits before they hit anything true.
- No confirmed public phone number and no public email anywhere. Both are
  bracketed as `[PHONE]` and `[BUSINESS EMAIL]` throughout every file in
  this repo and must never be replaced with an invented or "probably
  right" number. The Texan Drive-In, the other business in this batch,
  had a confirmed phone. Sheffield's does not. Do not let the two
  businesses' contact info blur together in any later loop.

## Conversion goal

Primary: get a first-time visitor to decide "yes, this is a real, open
place" and plan a visit (get directions, note the hours). Secondary: give
existing regulars a fast way to confirm hours and settle any doubt planted
by the Yellow Pages error. There is no purchase flow, no booking flow, and
v0 has no backend, so every "conversion" on this site is a decision made in
the visitor's head, not a form submission.

## Ideation: three directions, one chosen

**Direction A, rejected: "Cold Beer, Open Air."** Lead with the sensory
experience, screen walls, box fans, the feeling of shade on a Houston
afternoon. This is a real and good angle, but it is the angle any bar with
a patio can claim. It does not use Sheffield's actual asymmetric advantage,
which is 82 continuous years and a name people already recognize. It also
does nothing to address the closed-listing problem; it just describes a
mood and hopes the visitor already trusts the place is open.

**Direction B, rejected: "Houston's Best Kept Open Secret."** Lead with the
joke that nobody can find them online. Playful, and briefly tempting, but
wrong for this business specifically: a business currently fighting a false
"permanently closed" listing should never joke about being hard to find.
Self-deprecating humor about invisibility reads, to a worried first-time
visitor, as confirmation that something might actually be wrong. The tone
undercuts the one thing the site needs to do, which is state plainly that
the place is open.

**Direction C, chosen: "The Ledger."** Treat the site itself as the record
Sheffield's never got to keep online. Not a marketing microsite, a ledger:
the year it opened, the number of years since, plain confirmation of hours
and status, told in the flat, confident voice of a business that has never
needed to convince anyone before because everyone already knew. This
direction does three things the others don't: it uses the 82-year figure as
the site's actual spine rather than a footnote, it corrects the closed
listing by simply stating the true, current fact instead of arguing with
it, and it gives the visual designer a real, specific material world to
draw from, ice-house vernacular rendered as a kept record, not a rebuilt
diner set.

Full design lane and rationale for why it does not overlap the other four
businesses in this batch: see `design-system.md`.

# Implementation Brief for Loop 3 (Build Agent)

This file is the build prompt. Follow it exactly. Do not ask the human
follow-up questions before starting; every decision needed to ship v0 is
made below. If you hit a genuine ambiguity not covered here, make the
smallest reasonable call, note it in your PR description, and keep going.

## Stack

- Next.js App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS.
- shadcn/ui for primitives (button, card, separator, navigation-menu). Init
  with `npx shadcn@latest init`, then add only the components actually
  used, do not bulk-install the catalog.
- No backend, no database, no CMS for v0. All copy is hard-coded in the
  page files. There is no contact form that submits anywhere; see the
  Contact section below.
- Fonts: Big Shoulders Display, IBM Plex Sans, IBM Plex Mono, all via
  `next/font/google`. Do not link Google Fonts via a `<link>` tag.
- Icons: pick one library and use it exclusively, `@phosphor-icons/react`
  is the default choice (weights match the flat, unshowy tone). Do not
  hand-roll SVG icon paths. The one custom SVG this project needs is the
  ink-stamp mark described below, which is decoration, not an icon.
- Deploy target: static-friendly, no server actions, no API routes needed
  for v0.

## Design tokens

Implement exactly the six colors, three type roles, and spacing/motion
rules from `design-system.md`. Do not introduce a seventh color or a
fourth type role. Define tokens once, as Tailwind theme extensions or CSS
custom properties (pick one strategy, do not mix):

```
--screen-ink: #1C1E1A;
--slab-concrete: #B6AF9C;
--ledger-manila: #D9D2B9;
--patina-rust: #9C4A24;
--oxidized-screen: #56624A;
--chalkboard-chalk: #F2EEE2;
```

Light mode: background `--ledger-manila`, primary text `--screen-ink`.
Dark mode: background `--screen-ink`, primary text `--chalkboard-chalk`.
`--patina-rust` is the one accent in both modes, unchanged. Respect
`prefers-color-scheme`; do not force a single mode.

## Page structure

Four pages. See `page-plans/` for section-by-section detail on each.

1. `/` (Home) - `page-plans/home.md`
2. `/history` (About / The Ledger) - `page-plans/history.md`
3. `/menu` (What's Cold) - `page-plans/menu.md`
4. `/visit` (Hours, Directions, Contact) - `page-plans/visit.md`

Shared nav (all four pages, one line, max 72px tall): logo mark / wordmark
left, four links right (Home is implicit via logo, so nav shows History,
Menu, Visit), no hamburger needed at this link count but collapse to a
simple disclosure menu under 768px per the mobile rules below anyway, for
consistency with future page additions. Footer (all pages): address line,
hours summary, `[PHONE]` placeholder link, Yelp link, Facebook link,
one line stating "Sheffield's Ice House, open since 1942."

## Contact and unconfirmed data (hard rule)

There is no confirmed public phone number and no confirmed public email
for this business. Use the literal bracket placeholders `[PHONE]` and
`[BUSINESS EMAIL]` everywhere a contact detail would visibly appear to a
site visitor (footer, Visit page, any "Call us" button). Do not invent a
number. Do not mark either as a clickable `tel:`/`mailto:` link while it
is still a bracket placeholder, since that would ship a broken or fake
link; render it as plain text until the real business supplies the real
value, at which point swap in the real value and make it a working link.

**JSON-LD / structured data rule, non-negotiable:** if you add a
`LocalBusiness` (or `BarOrPub`) JSON-LD block for SEO, do **not** emit
`[PHONE]` or `[BUSINESS EMAIL]` as the literal string value of the
`telephone` or `email` fields. A search engine parses that as real,
garbage contact data, which is worse than having no phone/email field at
all. Instead, **omit the `telephone` and `email` fields from the JSON-LD
object entirely** until the real values are confirmed. Populate every
other field you can support with real, sourced data: `name`, `address`
(use the general Houston, TX location; do not invent a street address that
was not in the approved lead research), `url`, `sameAs` (Yelp and Facebook
URLs below), and `foundingDate` (1942). This omission is intentional and
is documented here so nobody "fixes" it by re-adding the bracket text
later.

Known public sources, safe to link directly:

- Yelp: `https://www.yelp.com/biz/sheffields-ice-house-houston-2`
- Facebook: `https://www.facebook.com/p/Sheffields-Ice-House-100063498222755/`

## Hours placeholder (extends the same honesty policy)

The approved lead research confirms no specific opening hours and no
confirmed street address, only "Houston, Texas" at the city level. Do not
invent plausible-sounding hours or a plausible-sounding street address to
fill space; that is the same category of error as inventing a phone
number. Use a literal `[HOURS]` placeholder anywhere hours would display
(the Home "Find Us" card, the Visit page hours column), styled like any
other ledger data point, and do not treat `[HOURS]` as a JSON-LD
`openingHours` value either (same omit-rather-than-fake rule as phone and
email). For the street address, do not fabricate one: use the
map-search link pattern below instead of a pinned address string.

## Map link pattern (no confirmed street address)

Since there is no confirmed street address, do not embed a map with
invented coordinates or a guessed address. Use a Google Maps search-query
URL, which resolves by business name and city without requiring a known
address:

```
https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Sheffield%27s+Ice+House+Houston+TX
```

This powers the "Find on Map" CTA on the Visit page and the "Find on Map"
button in the Home page's "Find Us" card. Once the owner confirms a real
street address, swap this for a proper embedded map or a direct
Maps-place link; note that upgrade path in the PR that first lands it.

## Menu content honesty rule

No confirmed, specific menu item list exists in the approved lead
research beyond "a recently refreshed menu" per Yelp (March 2026). Do not
invent specific dish names, prices, or a fake-precise menu to fill space.
The Menu page ships with honest category-level copy ("cold beer," "bar
snacks," "something off the fryer") explicitly framed as representative of
an ice house menu, not as Sheffield's confirmed current menu, with a
visible note that the owner should supply the real menu before this page
goes live publicly. See `page-plans/menu.md` for the exact copy and the
placement of that disclosure note.

## Hard performance and mobile rules

- Hero must fit the initial viewport on both mobile and desktop. Headline
  max 2 lines, subtext max 20 words and max 3 lines, primary CTA visible
  without scrolling.
- `min-h-[100dvh]` for the hero, never `h-screen`.
- Nav renders on one line at desktop, max 72px tall, collapses to a single
  disclosure/hamburger under 768px.
- Mobile breakpoint behavior is explicit per section in each page-plan
  file; every multi-column layout collapses to a strict single column
  (`w-full`, `px-4`) below 768px.
- LCP target < 2.5s: the hero's largest element is the display headline
  (text, not an image), so there is no hero image to preload or block on.
  If a hero background photo is used per `assets.md`, it must be
  `next/image` with `priority` and an explicit width/height to avoid CLS.
- INP < 200ms, CLS < 0.1. No layout-shifting web fonts: use
  `font-display: swap` behavior that `next/font` provides by default, and
  reserve space with the font's fallback metrics (next/font handles this
  automatically, do not override it).
- Only `transform` and `opacity` are animated anywhere on the site, per
  `design-system.md`'s motion notes. No `window.addEventListener('scroll')`
  anywhere.
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` disables the one hero settle animation;
  ship the reduced state, do not skip testing it.
- Lighthouse pass (mobile, throttled) before calling any page done.
- Dark mode and light mode both shipped and both tested, per
  `design-system.md`'s color mapping. Respect `prefers-color-scheme`, no
  forced single mode.
- One corner-radius system site-wide: `rounded-none` on containers and
  cards, `rounded-sm` on interactive controls only. No pill buttons.

## Definition of done for Loop 3

- All four pages built, responsive, both color modes tested.
- Zero em-dashes anywhere in shipped copy.
- Zero instances of a literal phone/email value other than the bracket
  placeholders in visible copy, and zero `telephone`/`email` keys in any
  JSON-LD block. Same rule for `[HOURS]`: no invented value, no
  `openingHours` key in JSON-LD until confirmed.
- Lighthouse mobile pass logged in the PR description.
- PR opened against `dev` per `github-workflow.md`, human review required
  before merge.

# Skills Used

Which skills were invoked for this Loop 2 pass, and what each one
actually changed in the output. Listed per file, not just as a flat list,
since the point of recording this is to show the work, not just claim it.

## `frontend-design`

Invoked before writing `design-system.md`. Contributed: the instruction
to ground every design choice in the subject's own material world
(screen mesh, concrete, garage-door openings) rather than a generic
"local business" template; the two-pass brainstorm-then-critique
structure that produced the three positioning directions in `brief.md`
before locking one in; the reminder that structural devices (the ledger
list on the History page) should only be used when the content is
genuinely sequential, which is why the ledger list format is confined to
`history.md` and not reused as decoration elsewhere.

## `design-taste-frontend`

Invoked alongside `frontend-design`, before and during `design-system.md`
and `implementation.md`. Contributed: the DESIGN_VARIANCE / MOTION_INTENSITY
/ VISUAL_DENSITY dial framework used explicitly in `design-system.md`; the
premium-consumer beige+brass+espresso palette ban, which is why the six
colors were deliberately pulled cooler and greyer than a default warm
cream-and-rust palette; the hero hard rules (headline length, subtext word
count, `pt-24` cap, `min-h-[100dvh]`) baked directly into `page-plans/home.md`
and `implementation.md`; the eyebrow-budget, zigzag-cap, and
no-duplicate-CTA-intent rules, which shaped the explicit layout-family
list at the top of every `page-plans/*.md` file and the "Get Directions"
label reuse documented in `user-flow.md`; the em-dash ban and the
fake-precise-number ban, which is why the Menu and History pages disclose
honestly instead of inventing dish names, prices, or founding-year detail
beyond what the lead research confirmed.

## `copywriting`

Invoked before drafting the actual sentences in every `page-plans/*.md`
file and in `brief.md`. Contributed: benefits-over-features framing (the
hero sells "come find out for yourself," not a feature list); the
one-idea-per-section discipline that kept each page-plan section to a
single job; the CTA formula (action verb plus what the visitor gets),
which produced "Get Directions" and "Find on Map" instead of a generic
"Learn More" or "Submit."

## `ogilvy`

Invoked immediately after the `copywriting` pass, specifically for
headline construction. Contributed: the rule that a headline should carry
the brand name, a promise, and news together, which is the direct source
of the Home headline "Sheffield's Ice House. Open Since 1942." (brand name
plus the news that it's still open, framed as the promise); the
instruction to treat the reader as intelligent and load copy with
specific facts rather than adjectives, which is why "82 years," "March
2026," and "Houston Press" appear as facts doing the persuading rather
than words like "amazing" or "beloved"; the instruction against burying
news, which is why the "Still Open" section states the closed-listing
correction as the second thing on the page, not hidden in a footer.

## `stop-slop`

Run as a final pass over every piece of prose in `brief.md`,
`design-system.md`, and every `page-plans/*.md` file before this repo was
committed. Removed: em-dashes (verified by grep, zero found across all
`.md` files at commit time), throat-clearing openers, adverbs, and the
binary-contrast sentence pattern ("not because X, because Y") that an
early draft of the History page disclosure line used before revision.

## `diagram-design` (considered, not invoked)

The task brief allowed either the `diagram-design` skill or a hand-written
flow description for `user-flow.md`. A four-page marketing site's flow is
simple enough that a hand-written ASCII flow in `user-flow.md` communicates
it faster than standing up an HTML/SVG artifact would, so the hand-written
option was taken. Noted here so the choice reads as deliberate, not
skipped.

All 10 required files present (page-plans/ contributing 4 page files for requirement #4). Repo created, verified, and pushed.

## Summary

**Repo:** https://github.com/PIIIX-org/texas-icehouse-sheffields-ice-house (private, default branch `dev`, `prod` branch created at the same initial commit, topics `web-lead`, `pending-beta`, `batch-1`, `geo-texas` — colon substitution noted in README.md)

**Design direction chosen: "The Ledger House."** The site treats itself as the public record Sheffield's never got to keep online: 82 years rendered as the literal spine of the homepage (a large ledger numeral, an ink-stamp "EST. 1942" signature mark), a dated ledger-entry list on the History page instead of prose, and a plain, undefensive tone that states the Yellow Pages "closed" error is wrong rather than joking about it. Palette is deliberately cool and industrial (`Screen Ink` near-black with a green undertone, `Slab Concrete` grey-tan, `Patina Rust` as the single accent, `Oxidized Screen` green) rather than the default warm cream+brass+espresso premium-consumer palette, and rejects teal/amber (claimed by The Texan Drive-In's Gulf Channel lane), high-plains dust tones (Robbins Nest), barn-dance wood/gold (Melody Ranch), and River Walk tile/terracotta (Texas T Pub) — `design-system.md` argues each distinction by name.

**Self-score: 91/100** (second pass; first draft scored 88, so I added explicit rejected-pages reasoning to `brief.md` and a consolidated component table to `implementation.md`, then verified repo hygiene against live `gh` output before finalizing):
- Positioning clarity: 9
- Unique visual direction: 9
- Strengths reflected on homepage: 9
- Weaknesses addressed: 9
- Page-by-page IA fit: 9
- Component inventory complete: 9
- Copy direction specific + correct locale: 9
- Asset list complete: 9
- implementation.md executable without questions: 9
- Repo hygiene: 10

**Contact-info confirmation:** grepped the full repo twice (before and after the second-pass edits) for em-dashes, phone-number patterns, and email patterns. Zero em-dashes, zero real phone numbers, zero real emails found. `[PHONE]`, `[BUSINESS EMAIL]`, and `[HOURS]` (an extra honesty placeholder I added for the equally-unconfirmed hours/address, documented in `implementation.md`) appear 21 times combined as literal bracket text, always as plain (non-linked) text, never as JSON-LD field values — `implementation.md` explicitly instructs omitting `telephone`/`email`/`openingHours` from structured data rather than emitting the brackets as fake values.
